status.note: First compound component in the library, and the first to own a keyboard model. The API is settled by ADR 0006; what is unproven is the composition mechanism — Tabs reads its items off `children`, and that has not met a consumer who wraps a TabItem yet.

intent.purpose: Holds one selection across a set of tabs and the panels they reveal, and owns the keyboard movement between them. It exists so that the selected state has exactly one home: the items compare against it rather than each holding a copy.
behaviour: Holds the selection, controlled via `value` + `onValueChange` or uncontrolled via `defaultValue`. Uncontrolled with no `defaultValue` starts on the first TabItem that is not disabled.
Renders its TabItem children inside a tablist, and its TabPanel children as siblings of it — a tablist may contain only tabs.
Moves between tabs on ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, jumps to the ends on Home and End, and wraps around at both ends. Disabled items are skipped.
Activates on focus: arrowing to a tab selects it in the same action. Suitable because every panel in this product is already in memory.
Calls `onValueChange` only when the selection actually changes. Re-clicking the selected tab does nothing.
Reads its items from `children` directly. A TabItem nested inside another element still renders and still works on click, but is invisible to the keyboard model.
notFor: A filter strip or view switcher with no panels behind it. Without panels this is not the tabs pattern; use a radio group or a nav, which say what they actually do.
Navigation between routes. These tabs show and hide content in place; they do not change the URL and nothing here manages history.
A vertical tab rail. Only a horizontal list is designed, and no orientation axis is exposed.
An accordion or disclosure set, where more than one section may be open. Exactly one tab is selected here, by construction.

a11y.keyboard: Tab reaches the selected tab only; ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move and select, Home/End jump to the ends, movement wraps and skips disabled items.
notes: Roving tabindex: exactly one TabItem is reachable with Tab, and it is the selected one. A controlled `value` that matches no rendered TabItem therefore leaves the whole list unreachable by keyboard. Nothing in this component detects that, because it cannot tell a not-yet-rendered value from a wrong one.

The tablist has no accessible name of its own. A consumer must pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, or assistive technology announces an unnamed set of tabs. This component cannot supply a sensible default and does not try.

Activation follows focus, so arrowing across the list changes the visible panel on every keypress. That is a deliberate choice for cheap panels — see ADR 0006 — and would be the wrong default for a panel that fetches.
Contrast is not applicable to this component: it paints only a hairline track. The contrast of a label belongs to TabItem.

children.description: TabItem children become the tab list; TabPanel children are rendered after it. Anything else is passed through untouched but takes no part in selection or keyboard movement.

root.description: The wrapper holding both the tab list and the panels, so the two stay adjacent in the DOM and a single className can position the pair.

list.description: The tablist itself. Carries the `track` — the hairline the whole width of the row that the selected item's indicator sits on top of.
